title: Keep the wallet's own error text off the console's Layer 1 (2 sites)
body:
## Summary
The console prints a wallet error's raw message in two places, while the stale banner over them is written never to.

## Description
apps/desktop/client/src/windows/main/console/Console.tsx:285 toasts `e.message` of every `wallet:error` (a CommandError from the wallet's fault stream, apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/native/events.rs:144); the Tumbler, for the same event, only goes stale (apps/desktop/client/src/windows/tumbler/Tumbler.tsx:253). apps/desktop/client/src/windows/main/console/Centre.tsx:82 renders `WalletNotice` with the failed read's error during the centre's loading state, and WalletNotice prints `error.message` (apps/desktop/client/src/shared/honesty.tsx:84). apps/desktop/client/src/windows/main/console/StaleBanner.tsx:4 states the rule ("Never a code, a command or an error's own text") and docs/ux/UX-GUIDE.md principle 3 forbids machinery words in any user-facing string. Fixed: both sites speak in the owner's words (the code word, STALE_PART for the part), never the message.

## Flow
- A get_settings read fails with message "settings store is busy"
- The banner says "Not available yet · your settings ..." (plain words)
- The centre under it says "Settings: settings store is busy" (the error text)
- Fix: Centre passes an owner-words `message` to WalletNotice; the wallet:error toast says a plain line, not e.message

## Expected impact
5

## Evaluation
Claim: user - one failure, one wording, no machinery text on Layer 1
Before: probe (console.test.tsx stale-banner case, extra assertion): .cs-centre.loading textContent = "The TableReading what needs you…Not available yetSettings: settings store is busy"; wallet:error toast = e.message verbatim (Console.tsx:285)
After: not built: the words are a copy choice; the instrument decides it
Method: probe - reproduced on the real App with the mock backend; After needs the chosen words
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: console.test.tsx: (a) h.failSettings -> expect(.cs-centre.loading text).not.toMatch(/busy/); (b) fire('wallet:error', {code:'UNAVAILABLE', message:'subscription stream closed'}) -> expect(.ui-toasts text).not.toContain('stream'). Both red today.

title: Give the stale banner's Try again a busy state
body:
## Summary
The stale banner's "Try again" stays an idle button while its reads run again, so a click looks like it did nothing until the reads settle.

## Description
apps/desktop/client/src/windows/main/console/StaleBanner.tsx:312-323: retry() fires refetch() on each failed World query and refetchQueries on failed displays, and the button never changes (no pending, no aria-busy, no words). Registry async-ui-states / action-busy-states: an action whose work is in flight says so on the control. Fixed: while any retried query is fetching, the button reads a "Trying again" word and is aria-busy/disabled; on failure the banner stays as now.

## Flow
- A read fails; the banner shows with Try again
- The owner clicks; the wallet is slow
- Today: no change until the read returns; a second click refires
- Fix: track fetching of the retried queries; show busy on the button

## Expected impact
4

## Evaluation
Claim: user - an in-flight retry is visible
Before: simulation: 3 walked cases (fast success: banner goes, fine; slow success: idle button for the whole wait; slow failure: idle button, then the same banner - indistinguishable from a dead click)
After: predicted: the slow cases show busy; falsified if the button cannot observe the refetch (each query exposes isFetching)
Method: simulation - needs a held read in console.test (the h.holdOpen pattern) to measure
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none
instrument: console.test.tsx: failSettings, then hold the next get_settings (promise gate), click Try again, expect the banner button aria-busy=true and disabled; release, expect the banner gone.

title: Tell the owner when a demo world could not be switched
body:
## Summary
When the demo choice cannot be stored, the overlay now lifts (30750d1) but nothing says why the world did not change.

## Description
apps/desktop/client/src/windows/main/console/DemoSwitch.tsx:26-31: applyDemo catches the localStorage failure and ends the switch; the owner is back where they were with no sentence. Registry async-ui-states / failure-states: a failure is spelled differently from a no-op. Fixed: a calm role=status note in the footer group (words in lib/words/demo.ts), cleared on the next open.

## Flow
- Desktop demo, storage blocked
- Owner picks Small shop
- Overlay shows, then lifts; same world, no word
- Fix: endSwitch carries a failed flag; DemoSwitch renders a not-stored sentence

## Expected impact
3

## Evaluation
Claim: user - a failed switch says so
Before: probe (demo.test.tsx, storage throwing): overlay lifts, 0 status text about the failure
After: not built: needs a new sentence (copy choice) that the demo words guard accepts
Method: probe - Before measured by the test added in 30750d1; After needs the words
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: DemoSwitch.tsx:30 try { localStorage.setItem(DEMO_KEY, formatDemo(next)); } catch { endSwitch(); return; }
instrument: demo.test.tsx 'a choice that cannot be stored...': add expect(screen.getByRole('status').textContent).toContain(<the new DEMO_SWITCH sentence>); red until built.

title: Order a module's Your call by the centre's queue order
body:
## Summary
ModuleLayer's default Your call takes the World's first need of the module (unsorted), while the centre and the waiting list use orderQueue/sortItems.

## Description
apps/desktop/client/src/windows/main/console/ModuleLayer.tsx:175-181 vs apps/desktop/client/src/windows/main/console/centreModel.ts:19. Hypothesis: the chip's "If you do nothing" could name a different decision than the first one the waiting list shows. REJECTED: the wallet already sends attention_list in sortItems order.

## Flow
- probe: attention_list on 3 mock worlds vs sortItems

## Expected impact
1

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the chip names the first decision of the waiting list
Before: default n=6, small n=2, large n=44: list order == sortItems order in 3/3 worlds; modules whose first need differs: 0/5, 0/2, 0/5
After: same (0 differences): churn
Method: probe - temporary vitest over mockBackend attention_list
Result: not-better
Gate: none
evidence: probe output: ["default n=6 same=true diffFirst=0/5", "?scale=small n=2 same=true diffFirst=0/2", "?scale=large n=44 same=true diffFirst=0/5"]
